reason: Checked the packet and the week-ahead tape. The book is already defensive at 49% cash after last week's trim, with JPM, ELV, CVX and XBI each down or flat by a few percent. CNBC's Oct 5-9 outlook shows a light calendar, with higher oil and higher yields as the drivers, and October Fed hike odds down from 68.6% to 24.9%, which eases the hawkish-Fed risk that drove the trim. Breadth is weak (about three-quarters of the S&P 500 lower on the week), so redeploying cash into more risk now is not obviously rewarded. Selling after small losses just before Q3 earnings (banks and managed care report from about Oct 13) would pay friction and lock in losses with no new information. CVX still benefits from elevated oil. Holding keeps the novelty-rule position intact too.
